common_name: Harlow Carr Witch Hazel (Golden RHS Garden-Bred Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Harlow Carr was raised at the RHS garden of the same name in North Yorkshire and flowers heaviest with at least a half day of direct sun.

directions: Harlow Carr smothers its bare winter branches in electric golden-yellow, ribbon-like petals set against a wine-red calyx, opening in mid to late winter with the lightly spicy fragrance typical of the best yellow intermedia hybrids. It builds a broadly upright to rounded frame reaching roughly 8 to 10 feet within fifteen years, somewhat more compact than older yellow selections. Mid-green summer foliage turns clear yellow in autumn before dropping to expose the coming season's flower buds. Grow in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil sheltered from harsh winter wind, and prune only lightly right after flowering.

common_name: Gimborn's Perfume Witch Hazel (Strongly Fragrant Late-Blooming Yellow Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, acidic to neutral, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; site near a path or window so the exceptionally strong fragrance can be enjoyed on still winter days.

directions: Named for the von Gimborn Arboretum in the Netherlands, this cultivar is prized above nearly all other intermedia witch hazels for the sheer carrying power of its scent, released from narrow, light-yellow petals backed by dark red sepals. It flowers later in winter than most yellow selections, often extending the witch hazel season into its final weeks, on a broad, rounded-spreading shrub that eventually reaches about 8 to 12 feet tall and wide. Mid-green leaves turn yellow in autumn before falling to reveal the winter flower buds. Grow in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, sheltered from drying wind.

common_name: Allgold Witch Hazel (Upright Yellow-Flowered Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Allgold forms a larger, more upright-spreading frame than many compact intermedia cultivars.

directions: Allgold bears clear yellow, spidery flowers on bare winter branches, lacking the reddish flush found at the base of many intermedia cultivars' petals, which gives its winter display a cleaner, more uniformly gold look from a distance. It grows into a larger, upright-spreading shrub than most yellow selections, eventually reaching 8 to 10 feet tall and 10 to 12 feet wide, and colors soft yellow in autumn before leaf drop. Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade, and prune only right after flowering since it blooms on old wood.

common_name: Arnhem Witch Hazel (Curled Orange-Red Fragrant Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic to neutral, well-drained soil in an open but sheltered site in full sun to partial shade.

directions: Arnhem, named for the Dutch city, opens narrow, strongly curled orange-red petals from red-brown sepals in late winter, with a light fragrance carrying on still days. It grows as a spreading deciduous shrub reaching roughly 8 to 13 feet in both height and spread over ten to twenty years, broader and more spreading than compact cultivars like 'Diane'. Mid-green oval leaves turn yellow and orange in autumn before dropping to expose the winter bloom. Grow in moderately fertile, well-drained, neutral to acid soil in full sun to partial shade, sheltered from exposed winter wind.

common_name: Amanon Witch Hazel (Twisted Yellow Lightly Scented Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, neutral to acidic, well-drained soil in a sheltered site in full sun to partial shade.

directions: Amanon produces long, narrow, gently twisted yellow petals rising from red-brown sepals, lightly scented and borne on bare stems in late winter. Its rounded, spreading habit matures to roughly 8 to 13 feet tall and wide over ten to twenty years, giving it a fuller silhouette than smaller-statured cultivars. Broadly oval mid-green leaves put on a strong autumn show of red, orange, and yellow before falling to reveal the winter flowers. Grow in neutral to acid, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, sheltered from harsh winter wind.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Sweetwater was discovered as a vigorous chance seedling on Long Island, New York.

directions: Sweetwater stands apart from most Pieris japonica selections for its genuinely sweet fragrance, released from dense, cascading clusters of white, lily-of-the-valley-like flowers that hold on the plant far longer than typical because the blooms are largely sterile and never go to seed. It grows notably more vigorously than seedling-grown Pieris, filling out into a full, densely leaved shrub with strong resistance to the leaf spot and lace bug problems that often trouble the species. Grow in moist, humus-rich, strongly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade sheltered from winter wind and harsh afternoon sun, mulching to conserve soil moisture and acidity.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade to dappled sun, sheltered from harsh afternoon sun and drying wind.

directions: Tiki forms a dense, multi-stemmed, naturally tidy mound to about 4 feet tall and wide, its symmetrical rounded shape needing little corrective pruning. Upright spikes of flower buds set in fall often take on a reddish hue and stand out against the glossy evergreen foliage through winter before opening into pure white, bell-shaped flowers that smother the plant in early spring. Its compact, uniform habit suits foundation plantings, low hedges, and shaded borders where larger Pieris cultivars would need frequent shaping. Grow in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, mulching to protect shallow roots.

common_name: Dodd's Crystal Cascade Falls Pieris (Fountain-Form White-Flowered Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial shade; this upright selection suits foundation plantings and woodland-edge borders.

directions: Dodd's Crystal Cascade Falls sends out fountain-like, cascading clusters of small, dainty, urn-shaped white flowers in early spring against consistently glossy, rich green foliage that holds its color well year-round. It grows into an upright, denser habit than many older Pieris japonica selections, reaching roughly 6 to 8 feet tall, making it useful as a foreground or foundation shrub as well as a specimen in open woodland plantings. Grow in moist, humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade, sheltered from winter wind and harsh afternoon sun.

common_name: Dodd's Pearl Falls Pieris (Tall Pendulous-Flowered Hedging Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil along shaded woodland edges or as an evergreen screen.

directions: Dodd's Pearl Falls carries long, pendulous flower buds that unfurl into cascading strands of white blossoms in early spring, on a taller, more heat- and humidity-tolerant plant than many older Pieris japonica selections. Reaching 6 to 8 feet tall, it is valued specifically as a dense evergreen privacy screen or hedge for shaded sites where few broadleaf evergreens perform as reliably. Grow in moist, humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade at a woodland edge or tree line, mulching to protect roots from summer heat.

common_name: Spring Snow Pieris (Fragrant Long-Blooming Hybrid Andromeda)
scientific_name: Pieris 'Spring Snow' (P. floribunda x P. japonica)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial shade; Spring Snow was bred by crossing P. floribunda with P. japonica and introduced by Briggs Nursery.

directions: Spring Snow combines the cold hardiness of mountain andromeda with the floriferousness of Japanese pieris, opening pink buds into fragrant pure white flowers on upright panicles that hold their display for a month or more, longer than most straight P. japonica cultivars. Its compact, mounding habit stays smaller and denser than many japonica selections, suiting tight foundation beds and rock gardens. Grow in moist, humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade, and avoid hot, exposed sites where the floribunda parentage is less heat-tolerant.

common_name: Shojo Pieris (Deep Pink Black-Budded Scarlet-New-Growth Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, strongly acidic soil in partial shade; Shojo is named for a red-faced mythical figure in Japanese folklore, a nod to its scarlet spring foliage.

directions: Shojo opens near-black flower buds into clusters of deep pink, lily-of-the-valley-shaped blossoms in early spring, a notably darker and more saturated pink than 'Valley Rose' or 'Pink Delight'. New spring foliage emerges a soft scarlet red before maturing to glossy dark green, giving the plant two distinct seasonal color displays. It forms a smaller, compact, mounded evergreen shrub than the species, well suited to foundation plantings and mixed shrub borders. Grow in moist, humus-rich, strongly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade, sheltered from harsh winter wind.
